strait.display_status: US NAVAL BLOCKADE OF IRANIAN PORTS CONTINUES (REIMPOSED JUL 14 20:00 GMT); IRAN'S JUL 28 MISSILE ATTACK BROKE THE PAUSE, US 'HEAVY WAVE' JUL 29, NO US STRIKES JUL 30-AUG 3; 20 VESSELS REDIRECTED, 2 DISABLED, 2 BOARDED (JUL 29); IRGC CLAIMED 2 TANKERS HIT AND 4 TURNED BACK JUL 31 (UNCONFIRMED); TRANSITS ~12/DAY VS >100 PRE-WAR; TRUMP CANCELED A PLANNED STRIKE AUG 1 AND ANNOUNCED TALKS — A DEAL WOULD REQUIRE 'COMPLETE AND TOTAL OPENING'; BRENT SLID TO ~$83
strait.status_timeline: Closed Mar 4, 2026 (IRGC); US naval blockade lifted and strait reopened toll-free Jun 18, 2026 (CENTCOM); reopening contested Jun 24-25 as IRGC reasserted permission-only transit and struck the Ever Lovely; four days of US-Iran kinetic exchange Jun 25-28 over the disputed transit route (Kiku struck Jun 27, US struck 14 Iranian targets Jun 26-27); 'stand-down for now' Jun 28-29 with free vessel movement; Doha talks announced Jun 30; ceasefire COLLAPSED Jul 7, 2026 (Iran struck 3 tankers); Trump declared ceasefire 'over' Jul 8; 5+ US strike waves on 300+ Iranian targets Jul 7-14 incl. first combat sea drones (Bandar Abbas, Jul 12); Iran hit 2 UAE tankers Jul 13-14; US naval blockade of Iranian ports REIMPOSED effective Jul 14, 20:00 GMT
strait.closure_method: Asymmetric denial via drone and missile strikes on commercial vessels, triggering insurance-driven shutdown. IRGC used sea drones, anti-ship missiles, and shore-launched projectiles to strike 21+ vessels since Feb 28. War risk insurance withdrawn or repriced at ~5% of vessel value — a 100x increase from pre-war 0.02-0.05%. For a $100M tanker, $5M per transit. At least one tanker paid $2M for transit rights through Iran-approved Larak Island corridor. Trump ordered DFC to provide $20B in political risk reinsurance (Chubb as lead underwriter), but JPMorgan estimates actual exposure at $352B across 329 tankers. Reports of naval mine deployment began ~March 10; US destroyed 44+ Iranian minelayers. Iran's stockpile estimated at 2,000-6,000 naval mines. Iran retains 80%+ of its small boats and minelayers. London Joint War Committee extended high-risk area to include waters around Oman.
strait.status: Day 163 (August 9): STRAIT EFFECTIVELY CLOSED AS TALKS GRIND ON AND IRAN HARDENS TERMS. The Aug 1-3 US strike pause held into a second week, with no new US strikes on Iranian territory Jul 30-Aug 9 (the longest quiet stretch since the Jul 7 collapse). As of Aug 8, CENTCOM's renewed blockade had redirected 51 commercial vessels and disabled 2 (up from 35/2 on Aug 2). An Iran-Oman framework for managing Strait traffic was reported near final, but the strait remains effectively closed and Iran's SNSC (secretary Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr) published new reopening preconditions Aug 8: lift the US naval blockade, withdraw US forces, permanently end the war, and pay war-damage compensation. A UAE/ADNOC oil tanker was struck by an Iranian missile and left burning in the US-supported shipping route Aug 8 (war-to-date 15 ADNOC vessels attacked, 1 crew killed and 20 injured, per CNN); Oman called its talks 'positive and constructive' but warned the vessel attacks threaten progress. US and Iran are passing messages via intermediaries, and CJCS Gen. Dan Caine reportedly told other advisers Washington needs an off-ramp (CNN, Aug 8). Brent ended the week near $83.55, down about 7% as Hormuz de-escalation hopes competed with the fresh attacks. Traffic remains crushed; treat any opening as unrealized until sustained transit counts recover. PRIOR — Day 157 (August 3): STRAIT CONTESTED — HORMUZ IS NOW THE CENTRAL TERM OF A PROPOSED DEAL. The pause that held July 24-27 broke on July 28, when the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at US forces in the region at 5:45 p.m. ET (all intercepted; Jordan downed five). CENTCOM answered with a 'heavy wave' completed 10 p.m. ET July 29 against dozens of IRGC targets, including coastal surveillance, coastal defense and maritime capabilities; Iran struck Jordan and Kuwait on July 30 (one killed in Kuwait). On July 31 the IRGC claimed it had hit two tankers transiting under US escort and forced four others to reverse course — UNVERIFIED: US and UK maritime security organizations did not confirm it, and Kpler still recorded two VLCCs exiting the Gulf that day. The blockade of Iranian ports continued throughout, with CENTCOM's redirected count rising to 20 vessels as of July 29 (2 disabled kinetically, 2 boarded, per UANI/CENTCOM). Then the direction reversed: after the US and Israel prepared what CBS sources called one of the harshest bombing campaigns of the war — against Iranian energy infrastructure — Trump said late August 1 he had canceled the attack because 'the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to,' and that the deal would include the 'Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT' alongside an end to Iran's nuclear threat. Iran's Mehr agency called the account 'simply a new lie' on August 2, and Tehran confirms no direct US talks; Trump nonetheless said on August 3 that negotiations would begin. Traffic remains crushed — roughly 12 transits August 3 (Windward: 5 inbound, 7 outbound, 6 running dark) and about 14 in 24 hours around July 28-29 (CNN/MarineTraffic), against more than 100 pre-war. Brent tracked the diplomacy rather than the fighting: $90.74 July 29, $90.12 July 31 to close a ~20% monthly gain, then a slump to roughly $83 on August 3. Treat the opening as unrealized until sustained transit counts recover. PRIOR — Day 150 (July 27): STRAIT CONTESTED — BLOCKADE HOLDS THROUGH A MUTUAL STRIKE PAUSE. CENTCOM completed its 13th consecutive night of strikes at 9 p.m. ET July 23 and then announced none on July 24, 25, 26 or 27; Iran halted retaliation after its July 24 IRGC salvo, and the mutual pause has held three days. The naval blockade of Iranian ports continues regardless: CENTCOM counted 9 vessels redirected and 1 disabled as of July 24, rising to 12 redirected, 2 disabled and 2 boarded by July 26. Iran is enforcing its own counter-regime — Iranian state TV said the IRGC navy stopped 6 vessels on July 27 for attempting routes Tehran had not approved. Transit management is now an explicit negotiating track: Iran and Oman held talks July 24-25 on a mechanism to manage Strait traffic, with Iran asserting the collapsed interim deal entitles it to manage the waterway and objecting to the US-supported Oman-side route. A regional official told AP on July 27 that Qatari- and Pakistani-led mediation had made 'significant' progress toward restoring the interim ceasefire, though an Al Jazeera mediator source said July 26 there was 'not much progress yet' amid 'fundamental differences' and 'deep mistrust' — treat the trajectory as unsettled. Traffic remains crushed at roughly 8 transits/day against more than 100 pre-war. Brent shed most of its war premium as the pause held, settling $88.36 July 27 (-8.7%, the biggest one-day drop since April 8) after touching $101.01 intraday July 23. PRIOR — Day 146 (July 23): STRAIT CONTESTED — US NAVAL BLOCKADE OF IRANIAN PORTS IN FORCE AND ACTIVELY ENFORCED. The blockade reimposed 20:00 GMT July 14 has been backed by a 12-night US strike campaign (through July 22-23). As of July 20 CENTCOM had redirected 7 commercial vessels and disabled 1 — the Curacao-flagged M/T Belma, hit with a Hellfire near Kharg Island July 15 (first vessel disabled under the resumed blockade) and re-struck by two missiles July 17; 9 vessels were redirected by July 22. 11th MEU Marines from the USS Boxer ARG boarded the tanker Wen Yao in the Gulf of Oman July 16, and a tanker on the Oman-side route sustained minor damage July 17 (UKMTO) — at least 9 ships have been attacked since July 6. US position (CENTCOM 'fact check' July 9; Rubio July 22): the strait is an international waterway Iran does not control, and strikes are to protect commercial shipping; Iran continues coercing vessels into its territorial waters. Transits fell to 8/day on July 16, a three-week low. A NEW second front opened when the Houthis declared (July 20) and enforced (July 22, striking the Saudi tankers Encelia and Layla) a Red Sea blockade of Saudi Arabia, putting the ~6.2M b/d that transits Bab el-Mandeb at risk and helping push Brent toward $100 intraday July 23. PRIOR — Day 137 (July 14, Tuesday): CEASEFIRE COLLAPSED — US BLOCKADE REIMPOSED, STRAIT STATUS CONTESTED. The June 28/29 stand-down broke on July 7 when the IRGC fired on three commercial vessels near the strait in Omani waters — the Qatari LNG carrier Al Rekayyat (engine room set afire), the Saudi crude tanker Wedyan (damaged) and a third vessel struck by a drone (UKMTO / Qatari & Saudi Foreign Ministries); no casualties. The US called it a 'gross violation' of the June 17 MOU, launched retaliatory strikes the same day and revoked the license authorizing Iranian oil sales; Trump declared the ceasefire 'over' on July 8 at the NATO summit in Ankara. CENTCOM then ran five-plus strike waves in seven days against 300+ Iranian targets concentrated on Iran's southern coast — air-defense systems, coastal radar, missile/drone sites, naval capabilities and IRGC small boats — including the first-ever US combat use of one-way attack sea drones (3 Saronic Corsair USVs) against the Bandar Abbas Naval Base submarine/ship-maintenance facility July 12. Iran hit two UAE-flagged tankers (al-Bahiya, Mombasa) with cruise missiles in Omani waters July 13-14, killing an Indian crew member and injuring 6 Indian and 2 Ukrainian crew (UAE Defense Ministry); the IRGC claimed it 'struck and disabled' two 'rogue supertankers,' and India summoned Iran's deputy ambassador. On July 13 Trump reimposed the naval blockade of Iranian ports (effective July 14, 20:00 GMT per the Joint Maritime Information Centre), declared the US 'THE GUARDIAN OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT' and demanded 20% reimbursement on all cargo — then reversed the fee within ~24 hours (July 14), replacing it with 'Trade and Investment Deals' from Gulf states and saying the strait is 'open to ALL Ship traffic except for Iran.' Brent settled +9.59% at $83.30 July 13, its biggest daily percentage gain since May 2020. STATUS DISPUTED: Iran declares the strait 'closed'; CENTCOM/JMIC say it remains open via the expanded southern (Omani-coast) route; threat level SEVERE. Functionally, transits collapsed ~52% week-on-week Jul 10-12 with 'defensive routing' dominant (Kpler/Lloyd's List Intelligence) — just 6 ships transited Sunday July 12 vs 108 crossings over the Jul 3-5 weekend; ~22 transits in the 24h before the blockade deadline (14 entering the Gulf: 11 cargo, 3 tankers); traffic is reverting to Iranian/dark routes and war-risk premiums are rising sharply. Iran's parliament introduced a Hormuz-management bill July 14. PRIOR — Day 129 (July 6, Monday): STAND-DOWN HELD ALL WEEK — TRANSITS RECOVERING, TOLLS DISPUTE ESCALATES. The June 29 stand-down held for the entire July 1-6 window: no new US/Israeli strikes on Iran, no new ship attacks, and no new IRGC or proxy strikes on US or Gulf targets. Transit traffic recovered — PortWatch counted ~27/day (last published June 28) rising to ~35/day by July 5, still well below the ~84-110/day pre-war norm; central traffic-separation lanes remain closed by ~80 naval mines, with two temporary corridors (a widened Omani-coast route and a northern Iranian route) carrying ~80/day combined. A five-vessel convoy led by the Liberia-flagged laden crude tanker HAFEET transited July 5 after ~8 vessels U-turned July 4 amid confusion over routing and tolls; Saudi exports ran ~90% of pre-war and the UAE was restored to pre-war (~3.9M bpd). The unresolved fault line is TOLLS: Iran said July 4 it will 'definitely' charge Hormuz transit fees once the MOU's toll-free window lapses (with 'special treatment' possible for friendly nations) and warned the UK and France; indirect US-Iran talks in Doha (July 1-2) left Hormuz tolls explicitly unresolved and are set to resume ~July 11 after Ayatollah Khamenei's state funeral. PRIOR — Day 123 (June 30, Tuesday): STAND-DOWN HOLDING AFTER FOUR DAYS OF STRIKES. The Hormuz transit corridor proved the central fault line of a sharp re-escalation: IRGC one-way attack drones struck the Singapore-flagged M/V EVER LOVELY (Jun 25) and the Panama-flagged tanker M/T KIKU (~2M bbl Qatari crude, Jun 27); in response CENTCOM struck 14 Iranian military targets across Jun 26-27 (4 targets near Sirik Jun 26; 10 targets in and near the strait Jun 27) — the first US kinetic strikes on Iranian soil since the Jun 17 MOU. Iran retaliated against Kuwait (Ali Al Salem AB, 2 ballistic missiles intercepted) and Bahrain (a Muharraq residential building hit) on Jun 28; a Qatari national was killed at sea by shrapnel (cause not formally attributed). UKMTO raised its threat level moderate→substantial Jun 27; ~60 IRGC high-speed craft were observed in the western strait Jun 27-28; 4 OFAC-sanctioned vessels transited simultaneously Jun 28 (Windward). On Jun 28-29 a senior US official said 'both sides will stand down for now and vessels can move freely' and 'we decided to stop all the kinetic activity'; Doha talks were announced for Jun 30 (Iran unconfirmed). The dispute is over which route ships use — the US/JMIC's widened bidirectional corridor near Oman vs Iran's IRGC-designated route near the Iranian coast. ~42 Hormuz transits were logged Jun 28 (28 inbound/14 outbound, Windward MIOC). PRIOR — Day 118 (June 25, Thursday): IRGC REASSERTS CONTROL AND STRIKES A SHIP — REOPENING NOW CONTESTED. After three days of surging traffic, the IRGC broadcast VHF Ch.16 warnings that vessels may transit 'only with Iranian permission' along Iranian-designated routes, calling unauthorized transits 'unacceptable and dangerous' and warning that ships running AIS-off or off-route 'carry the consequences.' Hours later an unknown projectile (likely a drone, per a maritime-security source) struck the Singapore-flagged container ship EVER LOVELY on its starboard side 7.5nm SE of Dahit, Oman, in the southern (Omani) corridor — bridge damaged, no casualties, no environmental impact (UKMTO/Ambrey); the ship continued onward. US officials attributed the strike to the IRGC (WSJ/CBS) — the FIRST ship attack since the June 17-18 reopening. On June 24 Oman and the UN IMO had announced a fee-free southern corridor; the IRGC rejected it, insisting on Iranian-designated routes, and the IMO then PAUSED its plan to evacuate ~11,000 seafarers still stranded around the Gulf. 3 oil tankers turned back and 3 diverted June 25 after the IRGC warnings (MarineTraffic via AP). Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority warned that unauthorized transits forfeit 'safe passage guarantees' and insurance coverage, and is reportedly seeking ~$40B/yr in 'security/environmental' fees once the 60-day free-passage window lapses (WSJ) — the MOU guarantees toll-free passage only through ~Aug 16. VP Vance said IRGC and US military reps would be posted in Doha as a direct de-confliction channel. Days 114-117 (June 21-24): TRAFFIC SURGED TOWARD THE PRE-WAR NORM AS THE WAR-RISK PREMIUM COLLAPSED. CBS logged ~35-36 ships/day June 22-23 ('busiest since the war'); Windward AI counted ~62 vessels June 24; UAE was exporting at ~85% of pre-war levels (IEA), though >500 vessels were still estimated waiting to exit the Gulf (vs the ~120-130/day pre-war baseline). The OFAC 60-day Iran oil sanctions waiver (General License X, June 22) and Brent's June 24 flip into bearish contango reinforced the unwinding; no attacks on shipping were reported June 20-24. Day 113 (June 20, Saturday): STRAIT REOPENING HOLDS BUT TRAFFIC THINS AS THE LEBANON FLARE-UP TESTS THE DEAL — with US equity markets closed June 19 (Juneteenth) and the Switzerland technical-talks ceremony cancelled, outbound Persian Gulf tanker departures stayed light into the weekend; no Iranian attacks on shipping reported in-window. The Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) continued advising transiting vessels to hug the Omani coast to reduce residual mine risk; mine-neutralization under the MOU (Iran to restore pre-war merchant traffic within 30 days) had not been independently verified. Day 112 (June 19, Friday): SWITZERLAND CEREMONY CANCELLED; HORMUZ TRAFFIC SLOWS. The Bürgenstock (near Lucerne) follow-on technical talks set for June 19 were called off (Swiss foreign ministry; VP Vance no longer traveling, citing logistics; Iran declined, insisting Lebanon fighting stop first). By Friday morning no outbound vessels were seen leaving the Persian Gulf amid the cancellation and Lebanon's deadliest post-MOU day; the toll-free 60-day regime (clock started June 18) remained in force. Iran signaled vessels would need mandatory war-risk insurance — currently free, possibly charged later. Day 111 (June 18, Thursday): US NAVAL BLOCKADE LIFTED — STRAIT REOPENS TOLL-FREE. CENTCOM announced 'all U.S. military blockade enforcement efforts have ceased' (the 14-point MOU's toll-free 60-day Hormuz clock started June 18 per VP Vance), while US warships 'remain in the general area' to police compliance — NO carrier withdrawal announced. Shipping resumed for the first time in ~110 days: Lloyd's List Intelligence logged major owners (Grimaldi, Cosco, Knutsen, NYK) transiting; Vance said >12.5 million barrels passed Wednesday night and ~10 million barrels transited or positioned Thursday, including the first Saudi-owned tankers since the war began. Iran's 'Persian Gulf Strait Authority' / 'Tehran Tollbooth' suspended charges for the 60-day window. EIA context: Hormuz oil flow averaged ~20M b/d in 2024 (~20% of global petroleum-liquids consumption); Q1 2026 flows had fallen to 14.6M b/d (down ~6M b/d year-on-year from 20.4M), the wartime disruption now unwinding. Day 110 (June 17, Wednesday): 14-POINT MOU TEXT RELEASED — HORMUZ STILL EFFECTIVELY CLOSED TWO DAYS BEFORE SIGNING. The published 14-point memorandum (Bloomberg/NBC/Time) commits to restoring Hormuz traffic to pre-war volume within 30 days of signing, Iranian removal of 'technical obstacles' and mine-neutralization within 30 days, and a US blockade lift on signing. Physical reality lags the political timeline: only ~7 ships have transited since the June 14 deal (MarineTraffic); 550+ vessels remain stranded; Windward logged ~24 vessels around the strait June 16 (16 in / 8 out, 11 'dark'); IMF PortWatch recorded 0 AIS transits June 14; TankerTrackers (June 17) reported the first Iranian crude exports in two months crossing the old blockade line. Crude transits run ~95% below pre-war and LNG ~99% below. A US military advisory (June 15) states the naval blockade 'remains in effect' until the June 19 signing ('Do not attempt to cross until explicit direction is given'). Mine clearance is estimated at 40–50 days (shipping/security sources) up to six months (Pentagon); Rubio (June 2) said Iran 'mined large segments of Hormuz.' Day 108 (June 15, Monday): HORMUZ REOPENING PENDING THE JUNE 19 SIGNING — at the G7 in Évian-les-Bains, France, Trump said the US–Iran deal is 'all signed' (a senior official confirmed Trump and VP Vance signed the MOU digitally) and that the Strait is 'partially open' now and will be 'completely open' and 'toll free' by Friday (June 19). Core deal terms: TOLL-FREE HORMUZ; US naval blockade LIFTED; Iran to clear mines within 30 days; ~$24–25B in frozen Iranian assets released; a 60-day nuclear-talks window. Iran's Deputy FM Gharibabadi countered that the strait closure CONTINUES until the deal is formally signed. Kpler lead freight analyst Matt Wright (June 15) projected tanker entries to the Persian Gulf could rise to ~12/day (~50% of prewar) in the first 30 days of the deal, with 118 tankers stuck in the Gulf able to exit within 15 days; AIS data showed traffic essentially unchanged pending the signing. Day 104–107 (June 11–14): Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central HQ declared the Strait FULLY CLOSED TO ALL VESSELS on June 11, threatening to fire on any ship, and the IRGC claimed it struck two vessels attempting transit (CENTCOM DENIED, saying the strait 'remains open for transit'). June 12–13: US forces downed Iranian one-way attack drones threatening commercial vessels near Hormuz, with CENTCOM saying the corridor remained open; NO Iranian attacks June 14–15. June 14: Trump declared the deal 'now complete' and authorized 'the toll free opening of the Strait of Hormuz, and… the immediate removal of the United States Naval blockade,' formal signing set for June 19 in Switzerland (Vance and envoy Witkoff for the US). CENTCOM blockade tally (as of June 14): 9 TANKERS DISABLED, 142 vessels REDIRECTED. The Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) had downgraded the Hormuz threat from 'critical' to 'severe' on June 7 'due to the number of safe transits conducted via the southern route' near Oman, while warning of an 'elevated risk of attack.' Day 103 (June 10, Wednesday): STRAIT REGIME UNCHANGED AND EFFECTIVELY CLOSED TO WESTERN-ALLIED SHIPPING AS THE WAR RE-ESCALATES OFF THE WATER — IRAN RETALIATES FOR THE JUNE 9 US STRIKES BY HITTING US BASES IN BAHRAIN (Fifth Fleet HQ — IRGC drones), KUWAIT (Ali Al Salem — drones) AND JORDAN (Azraq/Muwaffaq Salti — long-range ballistic missiles, ~1,000km, the war's DEEPEST IRANIAN REACH); all intercepted, no casualties or damage per US/Gulf officials. CENTCOM running blockade tally now: 8 TANKERS DISABLED, 134 vessels REDIRECTED, 42 HUMANITARIAN permitted. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright claimed Gulf vessel traffic was 'rising very meaningfully' — DISPUTED by independent shipping data showing Western-allied traffic still near zero. Day 102 (June 9, Tuesday): US ARMY AH-64 APACHE DOWNED OVER THE STRAIT (night June 8-9 local) — BOTH PILOTS RESCUED within ~2 hours by a US Navy 'Corsair' UNCREWED SURFACE VESSEL of 5th Fleet's Task Force 59 (a 24-ft Saronic-built autonomous boat, per CENTCOM Capt. Tim Hawkins via TWZ/DefenseScoop). US officials attribute the loss to an Iranian one-way attack drone; a mid-air collision was NOT ruled out, and Al Arabiya reported Iran told mediators it did NOT down the helicopter (CENTCOM: cause under investigation). Trump vowed to respond 'of necessity'; CENTCOM then launched self-defense strikes (5pm ET, concluded within ~4 hours) on Iranian air-defense, ground-control and surveillance-radar sites near the Strait. A US aircraft disabled the Palau-flagged M/T SETTEBELLO at 11:14pm — the 8TH vessel disabled under the blockade; 3 of 24 Indian crew went MISSING (Oman led search-and-rescue; the IMO chief condemned the strike). Day 101 (June 8, Monday): An F/A-18 from USS Abraham Lincoln disabled the Palau-flagged tanker M/T MARIVEX — the 7TH vessel disabled under the blockade — even as the first direct Iran-Israel ballistic-missile exchange since the April ceasefire unfolded off-theater (Iran's ~30-missile salvo on Israel; Israel's strikes on Tehran, Isfahan, Tabriz and a Mahshahr petrochemical complex). Day 100 (June 7, Sunday): WAR SETTLES INTO A BLOCKADE-PLUS-SKIRMISH EQUILIBRIUM CENTERED ON HORMUZ; STRAIT REMAINS EFFECTIVELY CLOSED TO WESTERN-ALLIED SHIPPING. WEEKEND OIL/EQUITY MARKETS CLOSED — carrying Friday June 5 closes forward (Brent $93.09, WTI $90.54); AAA national gas eased to $4.174/gal. REPEATING ESCALATION CYCLE JUNE 5-6: IRGC one-way attack drones harassed Hormuz shipping; CENTCOM downed the drones and struck Iranian coastal surveillance radar at Qeshm Island and Goruk; Iran then fired ballistic-missile and drone salvos at US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain (all intercepted, zero casualties). JUNE 5 (Day 98): CENTCOM shot down 4 IRGC drones headed toward the Strait; the IRGC fired warning shots near Larak Island and claimed it targeted 4 tankers attempting to 'violate its traffic-separation scheme' plus one vessel it named 'Panaya' (UNVERIFIED — CENTCOM says no US warships were hit). Iran condemned the US radar strikes as a 'clear violation' of the ceasefire. JUNE 6 (Day 99): CENTCOM downed 2 more IRGC drones near Hormuz (two-day total: 6). TRANSITS (Lloyd's List Intelligence): 40 vessels transited May 25-Jun 1 (May was the slowest traffic since the war began); 13 so far this week; a rise in 'dark' (AIS-off) transits; 142 non-Iranian ships have exited the strait since March, with Chinese-linked vessels ~25% of exits. EXPORTS (UANI May 2026 Tanker Tracker): Iran exported just 2.01M barrels in May (avg 64,921 bpd) — a 93% volume drop from April — valued at $219M (down 94%); UANI: 'No crude oil exports departed Iranian waters and successfully passed through the U.S. blockade.' Trump (June 6, Wisconsin) called the war 'largely finished ... one way or the other.' Day 97 (June 4, Thursday): STRAIT STAYS CONTESTED AND EFFECTIVELY CLOSED AS THE EARLY-JUNE ESCALATION COOLS SLIGHTLY — CENTCOM SAYS IT INTERCEPTED 'AN ADDITIONAL WAVE OF IRANIAN DRONES' THAT ATTEMPTED TO TARGET US FORCES IN KUWAIT (ALL INTERCEPTED; 'NO AMERICANS OR ASSETS HARMED'); IRAN'S NAVY CLAIMS IT TARGETED A US CENTCOM FACILITY 'RESPONSIBLE FOR RECENT US ACTIONS' — CENTCOM DENIES THE CLAIM (UNVERIFIED). Iran maintains its hold on the waterway while the US maintains its blockade of Iranian ports; tanker traffic stays at a tiny fraction of pre-war levels. EIA's Q1 2026 Global Energy Security Data report shows Hormuz oil/petroleum-liquids flows fell ~30% year-on-year to 14.6M b/d (from 20.4M b/d a year earlier); per UNCTAD/Kpler, average daily transits collapsed from 129 (Feb 1–27, 2026) to just 4 by March 7, 2026, against a historical daily average of 138 ships. OIL EASED on Israel-Lebanon ceasefire hopes — Brent ~$96.70 (−1.1% intraday), WTI ~$95.17 (−0.9% intraday); AAA national gas eased to $4.241/gal. Iran FM Abbas Araghchi (June 4) said talks made 'no progress' but channels remain open and defended the Gulf-state attacks as self-defense; chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned Tehran could abandon talks for 'confrontation' if Israeli strikes on Lebanon continue. The tentative 60-day US–Iran extension framework remains UNSIGNED. Day 96 (June 3, Wednesday): KINETIC EXCHANGES INTENSIFY AROUND HORMUZ AS THE CEASEFIRE STAYS 'TESTED' — US STRIKES AN IRANIAN OIL TANKER OFF QESHM (ENGINE-ROOM DAMAGE PER IRGC/TASNIM) AND CENTCOM SAYS IT FIRED AN AGM-114 HELLFIRE AT A TANKER 'ATTEMPTING TO BREACH THE BLOCKADE'; US DOWNS 3 ONE-WAY ATTACK DRONES TARGETING CIVILIAN SHIPPING; IRGC SAYS IT RETALIATED BY TARGETING A VESSEL IT NAMED 'PANAYA' AND WARNS THAT 'DISRUPTING THE SECURITY OF THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ WILL CARRY A HEAVY PRICE FOR THE US MILITARY.' Strait running at ~5% of the pre-war ~100/day baseline; the IMO traffic-separation lane is largely abandoned in favor of Iran's Iran-managed Larak Island corridor. Broader escalation: Iran's June 3 drone/missile strike on Kuwait International Airport killed 1 (an Indian national) and wounded 63+, with renewed attacks intercepted over Bahrain; the US House passed an Iran war-powers resolution 215-208. VP Vance: the ceasefire 'remains in place but the US reserves the right to launch defensive strikes'; SecDef Hegseth: 'for the most part, ceasefire means fire is ceasing.' The tentative 60-day US–Iran extension framework (reached May 24–28) remains UNSIGNED, with Iran's amendments outstanding. Day 95 (June 2, Tuesday): TALKS 'BACK ON TRACK' PER A REGIONAL SOURCE AS TRUMP TELLS ABC NEWS A HORMUZ-REOPENING / CEASEFIRE-EXTENSION DEAL IS REACHABLE 'OVER THE NEXT WEEK'; STRAIT REMAINS EFFECTIVELY CLOSED TO WESTERN-ALLIED COMMERCIAL SHIPPING — LLOYD'S LIST INTELLIGENCE ASSESSES NO WESTERN-ALLIED TRANSITS SINCE MAY 4. DISCREPANCY (flagged for reconciliation): AFP (June 1) reported ~70 commercial ships transited Hormuz over the prior three weeks 'with help from the U.S.' (escorts) — apparently distinct from the Lloyd's 'no Western-allied transits' assessment; the AFP figure likely counts U.S.-escorted / non-Western-flagged movements. impact.day_22_events: Day 22 — Nowruz/Eid — no operational pause. 8,000+ US targets, 8,000+ sorties, 130 vessels destroyed. Natanz struck. 5,000-lb bunker-busters on Hormuz coastal sites. Aerial campaign continues (A-10s, Apaches). Diego Garcia attacked from 2,500mi. Dimona struck. 9 salvos at Israel. 22 countries condemn closure. South Korea joins coalition. impact.day_23_events: Day 23 — Trump 48-hour ultimatum: 'obliterate power plants' if Hormuz not reopened by Mar 23 7:44 PM ET. Iran responds: threatens destruction of all regional energy infrastructure. CENTCOM Adm. Cooper video: 8,000+ targets, 130 vessels, Iran 'on steady decline.' GBU-72 destroys underground coastal missile facility. IDF 'wave of extensive strikes' on Hezbollah. USS Tripoli arrival imminent. Iraq force majeure on oilfields. Brent $112.19 (Fri close). Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline restarted 250K bpd. Japan offered safe passage — declined. Houthis warn but still inactive.
impact.day_24_events: Day 24 — Trump postpones power plant strikes 5 days, claims 'productive conversations' with Iran via intermediaries (Oman, Turkey, Egypt, Pakistan). Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf is key Iranian interlocutor — no direct talks, per Iran FM. Brent crashes 13.6% to $96.91 intraday (largest single-day swing of war) then recovers to ~$104. S&P surges +1.7-2.2%. IDF strikes Tehran; Iran strikes Netanya. Gulf states intercept fresh barrages. Saudi expels Iranian military attaché. Ford arrives Souda Bay for repairs. IEA: 44+ energy assets damaged across 9 countries, 'worst since combined 1973+1979.' 3,000+ vessels stranded. 600+ in immediate Gulf. $2M IRGC passage corridor. Houthis still dormant — ~30 tankers near Yanbu within range. New deadline ~Mar 28.
impact.day_26_events: Day 26 — 82nd Airborne deployment confirmed. 15-point ceasefire plan rejected by Iran as 'extremely maximalist and unreasonable.' Iran outlines 5-7 counter-conditions: closure of US bases in Gulf, reparations, Hormuz transit-fee arrangement, end to Israeli strikes on Hezbollah, lifting all sanctions, preservation of missile program. Iran's Hormuz letter to UN/IMO: 'non-hostile vessels' may transit after coordination; no passage for US/Israeli vessels. Brent $96.68 (−3.5%). S&P ~6,596 (+0.6%). Tripoli ARG in CENTCOM AOR. Boxer weeks out. Kuwait airport drone strike. Saudi intercepts 32+ drones. AP-NORC: 59% say war 'gone too far.' Speaker Johnson: 'almost done.'
impact.day_25_events: Day 25 — Iran launches 7 waves of ballistic missiles at Israel, 4 impacts in Tel Aviv, 6 wounded. IAF strikes 50+ targets overnight in Iran (IDF cumulative 3,000+). CENTCOM: 9,000+ targets, 140+ vessels destroyed, 9,000+ combat flights. 12+ underwater mines confirmed (Maham 3/7 types). CBS News confirms mine types. Kuwait alarms 7 times. Saudi intercepts ~20 drones. IRGC attacks US 5th Fleet in Bahrain — 1 Emirati KIA (first UAE combat death). UAE intercepts Abu Dhabi missile. Oil rebounds 3-4% to ~$103 Brent / ~$91 WTI after Iran denies all negotiations. Tripoli ARG enters CENTCOM AOR ~Mar 25. Lebanon expels Iran ambassador (deadline Mar 29). Israel DM Katz: occupy S. Lebanon to Litani. IDF strikes Beirut command centers. Pakistan emerging as lead mediator. Gas $3.956. ~$29.3B cumulative. Bahrain UNSC Chapter VII draft; France alternative. UK emergency meeting on economic fallout.
impact.day_27_events: Day 27 — Israel kills IRGC Navy Commander Tangsiri in Bandar Abbas precision strike — architect of Hormuz blockade eliminated. Senior IRGC naval leadership killed. Iran formally responds to 15-point plan with 5-point counterproposal including Hormuz sovereignty. Brent surges to $105.85 (+3.8-6.4%). Trump: 'get serious soon, before it is too late — NO TURNING BACK.' Confirms 4-6 week war. Reveals Iran allowed ~8 tankers through as gesture. IDF 'wave of extensive strikes' on Isfahan arms factories. Iranian missiles hit 4 Israeli locations. 2 killed Abu Dhabi from debris. Hezbollah rocket kills man in Nahariya. IDF soldier killed in Lebanon. Senate blocks war powers 53-47. Pakistan pushing in-person talks Mar 28. Gas $3.98 (+$1.00/month). Power plant deadline ~Mar 28. Iran fortifying Kharg Island. 82nd Airborne en route. ~$31.8B cumulative.
impact.day_28_events: Day 28 — Trump extends power plant deadline 10 days to Apr 6; G7 summit fractures — no communiqué; IDF overnight blitz Tehran/Kermanshah/Dezful; CENTCOM: 10,000+ targets, 130+ vessels, 8,000+ flights, 'largest navy elimination since WWII'; Iran submits 5-point counterproposal including Hormuz sovereignty; Pakistan pushes in-person Islamabad talks this weekend; Brent $108.01; VLCC rates $423,736/day all-time high; ~2,000 vessels stranded; 20,000 seafarers; insurance 5-10% of hull value; Iran mines (12+, Maham-3/7) + 1,500 drone boats; Philippines declares emergency
impact.day_29_events: Day 29 — BREAKING: Houthis launch first missile barrage at Israel — third active front opens; Bab al-Mandeb closure threatened — dual chokepoint scenario; ~30 tankers near Yanbu within Houthi range; Brent $112.57 (+4.22%); WTI intraday $100.04; Dow enters correction; VIX 31.05; Trump extends Hormuz deadline to Apr 6; VP Vance takes lead on negotiations; Iran rejects 15-point plan; 10 US troops injured Prince Sultan AB; Kuwait airport radar damaged; UK preparing coalition to reopen strait; ~$34.3B cumulative

impact.day_31_events: Day 31 — Trump threatens to 'completely obliterate' power plants, oil wells, Kharg Island, and desalination plants if no deal; Pentagon preparing 'weeks of ground operations' including Kharg Island raids; Brent $114.90-$116+ — +51% in March, steepest monthly surge on record; Dubai physical $126 — gap reflects acute physical supply stress; Iran agreed 20 Pakistani-flagged vessels through Strait (2/day); Iran 'tollbooth' charging ~$2M per transit in yuan; insurance 5%+ of vessel value; ~400 vessels stranded Gulf of Oman, ~20,000 seafarers; Islamabad summit: both sides 'expressed confidence in Pakistan'; Apr 6 deadline one week out; Iranian Navy Cmdr Irani threatens Lincoln directly; Spain closes airspace to US planes; $23B arms sales bypass Congress; ~$36.8B cumulative
impact.day_32_events: Day 32 — Iranian drone strikes Kuwaiti VLCC Al Salmi at Port of Dubai — risks major oil spill at critical commercial port; 2 Chinese container ships successfully transited Mar 30 (first cargo vessels since war began); Houthi deputy info minister: 'closing the Bab al-Mandeb Strait is among our options' — dual chokepoint scenario; Brent $112.78 settle, nearing $120 on Al Salmi attack; +~55% monthly — largest gain since inception 1988; Goldman: could exceed $147; SocGen: up to $150; IEA: 'largest supply disruption in history'; gas crossed $4.00 nationally; diesel $5.42; Jones Act waiver considered; WSJ: Trump may end war without securing Hormuz — 'not a core objective'; Apr 6 deadline approaching; 15-point US plan vs 5-point Iran counter — vast gap; ~$38.1B cumulative
impact.day_33_events: Day 33 — Trump claims Iran 'asked for CEASEFIRE' — markets surge (S&P +2.91%); Brent drops 5% to ~$105 on peace hopes; tanker Aqua 1 struck off Qatar by cruise missile (crew evacuated); Kuwait airport fuel depots ablaze from drones; IRGC cluster bomb hits Bnei Brak — children critically wounded; 3 missile waves at Israel; IRGC threatens 17 US corporate HQs; 200 dynamic strikes in 24 hrs; Hezbollah cmdr killed; Houthi missile intercepted; Apr 6 deadline 5 days; VLCC rates $423,736/day all-time high; ~400 vessels stranded Gulf of Oman; Mar 1-25: only 142 transits vs 2,652 in same 2025 period; Strait remains closed since Mar 4; Pakistan FM in Beijing — China as guarantor; Rubio: 'finish line coming'; Trump address 9 PM ET; gas $4.064 — record monthly jump; 15 KIA / 348 WIA; ~$39.3B cumulative
impact.day_34_events: Day 34 — Strait remains closed; 11 ships transited Mar 31 (Windward); Mar 1-25 transits fell 93% to 142 (USNI/Lloyd's); 71% of transiting ships Iran-linked; IRGC 'toll booth' at Larak Island charging up to $2M per crossing in yuan or crypto; war-risk insurance 5-10% of hull value; ~2,000 vessels and ~20,000 seafarers stranded; first LNG tanker (Omani-flagged Sohar LNG) attempting transit since war began (Bloomberg); UK-led 35-nation coalition convened to discuss reopening — US did not participate; Starmer: 'will not be easy'; Macron: military force 'unrealistic'; Iraq began exporting oil by tanker truck through Syria; Bush CSG ETA Apr 10-12; Apr 6 deadline 4 days away; Pakistan acknowledges 'obstacles'; China-Pakistan 5-point peace initiative; Brent $107.15 (+50.9% from pre-war); vessels attacked total 23

impact.day_36_events: Day 36 — BREAKTHROUGH: French CMA CGM container vessel (Maltese-flagged) successfully transited Apr 3 — first major Western European ship since hostilities; Japanese oil tanker followed hugging Omani coast; Iran selectively permitting China/India-bound vessels with escort; Pakistan secured deal for Pakistani-flagged ships; ~3,200 ships (~4% global tonnage) idle; 500+ waiting outside; IEA chief Birol: 'largest supply disruption in history — 12M bpd lost, more than two 1970s crises combined'; IEA largest-ever reserve release: 400M barrels across 32 members; Bloomberg Economics: Houthi Red Sea disruption could push oil to $140 — Saudi rerouted 5M bpd through Red Sea; Houthis 4 attacks in 7 days on Israel, holding fire on shipping but threatening Bab al-Mandeb blockade of 'aggressor countries'; Pakistan ceasefire talks collapsed; F-15E shot down (first US combat aircraft loss since 2003); Apr 6 deadline 2 days; Trump threatens to bomb Iran 'back to Stone Ages'; Brent $109.03
impact.day_37_events: Day 37 — April 6 ultimatum less than 24 hours away — Trump: 'Tuesday will be Power Plant Day, and Bridge Day, all wrapped up in one'; Sen. Graham confirms Trump intends to follow through with 'overwhelming military force'; Iran rejects ultimatum — Gen. impact.day_38_events: Day 38 — Trump sets Apr 7 8 PM ET deadline for Iran to reopen Strait or face strikes on power plants and bridges; 45-day ceasefire proposal from Egyptian-Pakistani-Turkish mediators rejected by Iran — 'incompatible with ultimatums and threats'; OPEC+ agreed Apr 5 to increase output 206K bpd for May — analysts dismiss as 'academic' (less than 2% of disrupted supply); Lloyd's List: 53 transits last week up from 36 — still 90%+ below normal; 400+ vessels anchored Gulf of Oman; QatarEnergy force majeure since Mar 4; 20,000+ seafarers stranded; Brent ~$111.25; JPMorgan warns $150+; some model $200/bbl; Houthis have not yet resumed Red Sea shipping attacks — holding as strategic card; Houthi leader warns Bab al-Mandeb could be closed if Gulf Arab states join war; Trump admitted arming Iranian Kurdish groups; markets reopen Monday after Easter
impact.day_40_events: Day 40 — CEASEFIRE RALLY THEN FRACTURE: Apr 8 ceasefire rally — Brent closes $94.75 (-14%), WTI $94.41 (-16%, biggest drop since Apr 2020); S&P 6,782.81 (+2.51%), Dow +2.85% best day since Apr 2025; VIX 21.04 (-18.39%); Apr 7: 11 vessels transited via IRGC-controlled Northern Corridor. IRGC re-closes Hormuz in response. Apr 8: only 5 bulk carriers outbound by noon — NO major oil tankers. White House (Leavitt) claims strait 'open' — Bloomberg, CNBC, Windward contradict. Netanyahu confirms ceasefire excludes Lebanon. European leaders + EU demand inclusion. ~800 tankers, 3,200 total vessels stuck in Gulf. CENTCOM Apr 8: 13,000+ targets, 80% Iran air defenses destroyed, every sub sunk, 97% mines eliminated.
impact.day_41_events: Day 41 — CEASEFIRE 'ON VERGE OF COLLAPSE' (Soufan Center): Brent rebounds to ~$97-98; WTI rebounds to ~$97-98; $12-18 Hormuz risk premium re-embedded; S&P reverses intraday from 6,782.81 close to ~6,752.64; VIX climbs toward 23-26; Hezbollah launches retaliatory missiles on northern Israel early Apr 9; Iran parliamentary speaker formally accuses US of ceasefire breach; Windward: 'supervised pause, not reopened'; White House confirms Vance + Witkoff + Kushner for Islamabad talks Apr 10-11 (highest-level US-Iran engagement since 1979); Bush CSG ETA Apr 10-12; Pope Leo XIV Apr 11 peace vigil at St. Peter's; Hegseth/Caine: US forces remain; Trump CNBC: military ready for 'next conquest'; UN Human Rights Chief: Lebanon strikes 'nothing short of horrific'; Soufan Center April 9 headline: 'Already Tenuous Ceasefire in Iran Hovers on the Verge of Collapse.'
impact.day_42_events: Day 42 — CEASEFIRE ~72 HOURS — VANCE DEPARTS FOR ISLAMABAD: ADNOC CEO Sultan Al Jaber: 'The Strait of Hormuz is not open. Access is being restricted, conditioned and controlled.' Hegseth contradicts: 'the strait is open.' Only ~15 ships transited in first 48 hours vs pre-war ~110/day. 600+ vessels stranded including 325 loaded tankers (Lloyd's List Intelligence) with ~20,000 seafarers. Iran demanding military approval for each vessel and planning tolls exceeding $1M/ship. Iran released map indicating possible mining with designated shipping lanes. US Navy decommissioned last 4 Avenger-class minesweepers from Bahrain Jan 2026; defense officials told WSJ Navy escorts 'aren't currently feasible' — Strait described as Iranian 'kill box.' VP Vance departed for Islamabad with Witkoff + Kushner — highest-level US-Iran engagement since 1979; formal talks Saturday Apr 12. Iran delegation: Ghalibaf + Araghchi. Iran's Parliament Speaker says 3/10 ceasefire points violated. Brent eases to ~$96; WTI ~$98. S&P 6,824.66 (Apr 9 close +0.62%). Bush CSG ETA today-Sunday — dual-carrier capability. March CPI released. Macron says ~15 countries mobilized for defensive mission to reopen Hormuz. Pope vigil tomorrow. 60-day War Powers deadline Apr 29.
impact.day_43_events: Day 43 — ISLAMABAD TALKS BEGIN — 'TEHRAN TOLLBOOTH': First direct US-Iran face-to-face since 1979 at Serena Hotel — VP Vance, Witkoff, Kushner meet Ghalibaf + Araghchi. Hormuz reopening central to negotiations. IRGC established 'Tehran Tollbooth' — alternative channel north of Larak Island requiring prior permission, charging up to $2M/vessel (yuan or crypto), capping at 15 ships/day. Only ~10-16 ships transited in first 3 days post-ceasefire vs ~135/day pre-war. 500-700 vessels over 10,000 DWT stranded (Lloyd's List); 325 tankers; 230 oil-laden ready to sail (ADNOC). 20,000+ seafarers aboard. War risk insurance ~8x pre-war. All 12 P&I clubs withdrew coverage — 'de facto closure by insurance.' Physical dated Brent traded at $131.97/bbl — $35 premium over futures ($96.66) reflecting extreme physical scarcity. 13M bpd shut in (Energy Aspects). TD Securities: ~1 billion barrels lost by end of April. Iran's 10-point plan demands Hormuz transit fees ratified in binding UNSC resolution. US demands unconditional reopening. Disputed frozen assets: Iran claims US agreed to release — US flatly denies. CNN: China preparing new air defense delivery to Iran. Bush CSG approaching Gibraltar — ETA Red Sea Apr 14-18. Pope Leo XIV peace vigil noon ET. Congress returns Apr 14. 60-day War Powers deadline Apr 29.
impact.day_44_events: Day 44 — TRUMP DECLARES US NAVAL BLOCKADE OF HORMUZ: Islamabad talks collapsed after 21 hours Apr 12 with no agreement. Vance press conference: 'We have not reached an agreement' — identifies nuclear enrichment as core sticking point, leaves 'final and best offer.' Five gaps: nuclear, Hormuz, Lebanon, sanctions/frozen assets, reparations. Araghchi and Witkoff 'nearly came to blows' during Hormuz discussions (Turkish media). Ghalibaf five-point X post blames US: 'the other side was ultimately unable to gain the trust of the Iranian delegation.' Trump immediately announces blockade via Truth Social: 'Effective immediately, the United States Navy, the Finest in the World, will begin the process of BLOCKADING any and all Ships trying to enter, or leave, the Strait of Hormuz.' Orders Navy to interdict every vessel that paid Iran's toll, destroy Iranian mines. Threatens: 'Any Iranian who fires at us, or at peaceful vessels, will be BLOWN TO HELL!' / 'At an appropriate moment, we are fully LOCKED AND LOADED, and our Military will finish up the little that is left of Iran!' Iran's deputy parliament speaker Nikzad: victory determined by 'the will of nations... not by rhetoric on social media.' KEY COMPLICATION: Iran reportedly lost track of mines it planted. ANOTHER: Chinese, Indian, and Pakistani ships transiting under Iranian deals could escalate into broader confrontation. Ceasefire on Iran front technically holds ~120 hours (expires ~Apr 22) but future uncertain. Historic Apr 11 precedent: USS Frank E. Petersen Jr. (DDG-121) and USS Michael Murphy (DDG-112) transited Strait for mine-clearing — first US warships since war began. Bush CSG at/approaching Gibraltar — ETA Red Sea Apr 14-18. Markets closed weekend — Monday reopening expected to reverse much of last week's ceasefire rally.
impact.day_45_events: Day 45 — BLOCKADE EFFECTIVE 14:00 GMT — IRGC WARNS OF 'HARSH AND DECISIVE' FORCE: Trump's US naval blockade takes effect April 13 14:00 GMT, approximately 24 hours after Islamabad talks collapsed. CRITICAL DIVERGENCE: Trump's Truth Social declaration threatened all Hormuz traffic, but CENTCOM's operational order narrowed scope — blockade applies only to ships entering or exiting Iranian ports and 'will not impede freedom of navigation for vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz to and from non-Iranian ports.' IRGC warned military vessels approaching the Strait 'will be considered a violation of the ceasefire and will be met with severe force.' Iran's armed forces called the blockade 'an illegal act amounting to piracy.' IRGC: 'Security in the Persian Gulf and the Sea of Oman is either for everyone or for NO ONE.' Ghalibaf taunts: 'Soon you'll be nostalgic for $4-$5 gas.' UK explicitly declines — Starmer: 'not getting dragged into the war.' Australia not asked. EU's von der Leyen: EU fossil fuel import costs +€22B in 44 days. CENTCOM announces 'additional U.S. forces, including underwater drones, will join the clearance effort.' WSJ Apr 13: 60%+ of IRGC's naval fleet tasked with Hormuz patrol remains intact — contradicts White House 97% mine elimination claim. Oil surged back above $100: Brent ~$103 (+7.3%), WTI $97-105 intraday. S&P ~6,775-6,781 (-0.5-0.6%); VIX 21.30 (+10.8%). Trump says ceasefire 'holding well,' 'their military is destroyed, their whole navy is under water' — zero new Iranian casualties since Apr 7 (ceasefire ~144 hours). Lavan Oil Refinery Apr 11 remains most recent alleged violation (unclear attribution). Next 48 hours: most dangerous since Apr 7 ceasefire. Ceasefire expires ~Apr 21.
